sentences.text: This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 2636 Bigha 18 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme'
under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
LAC no. 476/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Mittara Sain & Anr. Vs. Union of India Page no. 2 of 12 3.

The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2636 Bighas 18 Biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/
per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are the recorded owner/bhumidhar of the land comprised in Khasra no. 17//1 (406) i.e. total area measuring 4 Bigha and 06 Biswas, having share as per the revenue record, situated in the revenue estate of Village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari), Delhi (in short, the said land).
5.

The petitioner aggrieved by the market value determined by the LAC, vide the subject award announced on 06.02.2006 while accepting the compensation under protest, challenged the said Award on the grounds as detailed in the reference petition which are summarized as under: -
(i) The ld. LAC has not adopted the correct method of valuation.

The market value as assessed by Land Acquisition Collector is imaginary and LAC no. 476/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Mittara Sain & Anr. Vs. Union of India Page no. 3 of 12 based upon the Govt. Policy.

sentences.text: The market value of the acquired land and the market value of the construction/ structure can't be fixed on the basis of any such policy of the Government.
The market value of the acquired land is to be assessed strictly as provided by law within the purview of Section 23 and 24 of Land Acquisition Act.

(iii) The Land Acquisition Collector have not taken into consideration the future potentiality of the land and should have determined the market value by keeping in view the market value as fixed by the Government for allotment of residential plots/ flats.

The Ld. LAC should have adjusted some Mittara Sain (2505-06) vs Union Of India (Kirari Suleman Nager) on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196059574/

(iv) The DDA with the approval of Govt. of India had issued the guidelines through which DDA has increased the rate of alternative plots from Rs. 750/- per sq. yards to Rs. 5,000/- (approx) per sq.
yards.
Therefore, the said land of the petitioner has higher potential value than is assessed by the Ld. LAC.
Further the land of the petitioner is very fertile and leveled and it gives commercial crops 2-3 in a year and yielded high income for the petitioners, without any depression or defect.
Therefore, the said land hardly needs any development to be done to make it fit for use as a developed site and it can be used for industrial, commercial or residential use with very little efforts.

(iv) All the amentities and facilities of life like water, electricity, metalled roads, general market, post office, transport facilities, banking facility, hospitals, Engg. College, schools, telephone exchange,
police station are LAC no. 476/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Mittara Sain & Anr. Vs.
Union of India Page no. 4 of 12 very near to GTK Road, Rohtak Road, Narela Anaj Mandi adjacent to the Narela township which was urbanized in the year 1922 and having commercial as well as Narela industrial area is very near Bawana Industrial Area much prior to the date of notification U/s 4 of the Act but the LAC did not consider this fact while passing the said award.
(v) There are many palatial farm houses in the close vicinity of the revenue estate of Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari).

The cost of the land of these farmhouses is not less than Rs. 15,000/- sq. yards which also increases the marketable value of the land of the petitioner and the said land is situated on the main road.
The LAC, while passing the award, did not assess the correct value of the standing trees.

(vi) Further, the LAC has ignored the future prospects and possibilities of fetching much higher price by the land, other well developed colonies and full approved Industrial areas, etc where the minimum market value of the land is Rs. 10,000/- per sq. yards.

Therefore, the compensation according to the value of land should be valued at Rs. 10,000/- per sq. yards which is the fair actual value of land of the land on the date of notification U/s 4 (1) of the Land Acquisition Act.
(vii) The LAC has also erred in not awarding the compensation for the expenses, loss and injury sustained by the petitioner due to competed change of nature and place of business/ livelihood.

The LAC has also not considered the yearly increase of 12% per annum in the value of land between 01.04.2001 to 21.03.2003 i.e. date of policy announced vide order no.F9(20)/L&B/LA/6696 dated 09.08.2001 and the government has also LAC no. 476/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW))

14. The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.

(2) Additional amount @ 12% (
in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).
(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
LAC no. 476/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Mittara Sain & Anr. Vs. Union of India Page no. 11 of 12 21.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
